items.label: What it can access
items.text: The assistant connects with your {{jval .PortalName}} account and can use the same files, uploads, and settings you see when you sign in yourself.

items.label: What gets shared
items.text: To answer your questions, the assistant may send parts of your conversation to this server, including anything you've typed into the chat. Don't share the link or your account with an app you don't trust.

items.label: Trust the link
items.text: This is the official {{jval .PortalName}} server, run by LumeWeb. ChatGPT, Claude, and similar apps can't check a server link for you, so only add a link you got from this page.

platforms.label: Grok
platforms.note: On Grok Business or Enterprise a team admin has to set up the connector in the cloud console before anyone can use it.

steps.title: Fill in the Custom Connector dialog

subSteps.title: Name it
subSteps.detail: Something like {{jval .PortalName}} works.

subSteps.title: Paste the server link
subSteps.detail: In the Server URL field, from the card above.

subSteps.title: Click Add Connector
subSteps.detail: Grok saves the connector as soon as it checks the link.

subSteps.title: Approve access
subSteps.detail: Approving lets Grok use your {{jval .PortalName}} account: the same files and settings you see when you sign in yourself.

steps.title: Start chatting
steps.detail: Grok uses {{jval .PortalName}} when you ask it to.

platforms.label: Claude
platforms.note: Custom connectors using remote MCP work on all Claude plans; Free is limited to one. On Team or Enterprise only an owner can add them. You only need a name and the server link; ignore the technical options Claude shows along the way.

steps.title: Open Claude's connector settings
steps.detail: This link opens the Add custom connector dialog directly.

steps.title: Fill in the Add custom connector dialog

subSteps.title: Name it
subSteps.detail: Something like {{jval .PortalName}} works.

subSteps.title: Paste the server link
subSteps.detail: In the Remote MCP server URL field, from the card above.

subSteps.title: Click Continue
subSteps.detail: Claude checks the link and shows the settings it detected.

subSteps.title: Keep what Claude detected
subSteps.detail: Authentication stays on 'Always required' and OAuth client on 'Use Anthropic's hosted client metadata' (Recommended). Don't add request headers or open Advanced; those are for people building their own servers.

steps.title: Allow the {{jval .AllowDomain}} domain
steps.detail: Claude won't ask for this, so add it ahead of time in the allowed domains setting.

subSteps.title: Open the allowed domains setting
subSteps.detail: In Claude, go to Settings, then the allowed domains list (or your workspace's connector settings).

subSteps.title: Add {{jval .AllowDomain}}
subSteps.detail: Enter the domain exactly as shown on the card above.

subSteps.title: Save
subSteps.detail: Confirm the change before you continue.

steps.title: Connect and sign in
steps.detail: Back on the Connectors page, click Connect on your new connector. Connecting lets Claude use your {{jval .PortalName}} account: the same files and settings you see when you sign in yourself. If a sign-in page shows extra fields or settings you don't recognize, leave them blank; Claude signs you in with your {{jval .PortalName}} account.

platforms.label: ChatGPT
platforms.note: Custom MCP connectors work on paid ChatGPT plans, including Pro. On Business, Enterprise, and EDU they're in beta, so a workspace admin has to switch on Developer mode and approve the connector before anyone can use it.

subSteps.title: Turn it on for your account
subSteps.detail: Open Settings, then Apps and Advanced settings, and switch on Developer mode.

subSteps.title: Workspace with an admin? They enable it
subSteps.detail: In the admin settings: Permissions and roles, Connected data, then the Developer mode switch.

steps.title: Open Apps and create a connector
steps.detail: Go to Settings, then Apps, and click Create. The New Plugin dialog opens.

steps.title: Fill in the New Plugin dialog

subSteps.title: Name it
subSteps.detail: Something like {{jval .PortalName}} works. The icon and description are optional.

subSteps.title: Paste the server link
subSteps.detail: Under Connection, keep Server URL selected and paste the /mcp link from the card above.

subSteps.title: Leave Authentication on OAuth
subSteps.detail: ChatGPT discovers these settings on its own once the link is valid. Nothing to enter.

subSteps.title: Tick the risk checkbox
subSteps.detail: ChatGPT shows this because it can't check custom server links; whatever you add, it sends parts of your chats to that server. The link on this page is the official {{jval .PortalName}} server, so this one is safe. Tick 'I understand and want to continue' to unlock Create.

subSteps.title: Click Create
subSteps.detail: The connector appears as a draft.

subSteps.title: Wait for the scan
subSteps.detail: Approve sign-in if it opens.

subSteps.title: Admins: publish it
subSteps.detail: Go to Workspace settings, Apps, Drafts, then Publish.

subSteps.title: Everyone else: get it approved
subSteps.detail: An admin has to publish before you can use it.

subSteps.title: Pick the connector from the = menu
subSteps.detail: In the chat, open the = icon's menu and pick the connector.

platforms.label: Other apps
platforms.note: Use the full link that ends in /mcp; the bare address is this help page, not the server. If something fails, try signing in again, or double-check the link and the connection type.

steps.title: Add a server
steps.detail: Most apps let you add a server under their apps or integrations settings.

steps.title: Choose the web option, paste the link

subSteps.title: Paste the server link
subSteps.detail: From the card above.

steps.title: Sign in when prompted
steps.detail: Connecting opens a sign-in page for your {{jval .PortalName}} account.

steps.title: Approve access
steps.detail: Allow access so it can connect. Approving gives the app your {{jval .PortalName}} account, so only do this for a server link you got from this page or another source you trust.

steps.title: Check it works
steps.detail: Make sure the tools show up, then use them in a conversation.
